problem_markdown: Prove no function $f:\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ satisfies $f(f(n))=n+1987$ for every $n\ge0$.
solutions_markdown:
Suppose such an $f$ exists and let $N=\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. The equation makes $f$ injective: equal values at $m,n$ would imply $m+1987=n+1987$.

Put $A=N\setminus f(N)$. Injectivity implies
$$f(A)=f(N)\setminus f(f(N)).$$
Indeed, the image of a point outside $f(N)$ cannot coincide with the image of a point inside $f(N)$, and every element of the displayed difference has such a preimage.

Consequently the disjoint sets $A,f(A)$ partition $N\setminus f(f(N))=\{0,1,\ldots,1986\}$. They are finite and have equal cardinality because $f$ is injective. Their union must therefore have even cardinality, contradicting its size 1987.
